model.name: Dataset
model.purpose: Describe a dataset as a catalogued, identifiable data asset so that an agent can register it, understand its scope and structure, serve it through distributions and services, judge its quality and fitness, and govern its rights, versions and retirement independently of storage format or interface.
model.scope_statement: WM-DAT-001 covers the asset-level semantics of a dataset: identity and designation, catalogue registration, classification, scope and coverage, declared structure, distributions and access services, rights and accountability, provenance, versioning and retirement, quality and fitness evidence, and profile-level interoperability. It treats DCAT 3, DCAT-AP, DCAT-US, schema.org/Dataset, DataCite, Data Package, RO-Crate, Croissant, DQV and PROV-O as alignments, not as the model's own semantics. It stops at the boundary of the data content itself: the meaning of individual variables, the full derivation graph, the full quality assessment apparatus and the commercial offering wrapped around the data belong to sibling models.
in_scope: Dataset identity, persistent identifiers and designation (title, description, language)
Catalogue record and registration state, distinct from the dataset it describes
Thematic classification, keywords and controlled-vocabulary terms
Scope and coverage: observation unit, granularity, temporal and spatial extent
Declared schema reference, data dictionary pointer and dataset series membership
Distributions: format, media type, byte size, checksum, packaging profile
Access services, endpoints, protocols and access conditions including embargo
Licence, rights statement, use restrictions and machine-readable policy
Holder, publisher, creator, contact point and steward accountability
Personal and sensitive data controls at asset level
Source lineage, production method and processing summary
Version identity, change record, release cadence and status
Deprecation, withdrawal, tombstoning, retention and deletion
Quality measurements, fitness-for-use statements and known limitations
ML training readiness and dataset documentation for AI use
Application profile conformance, validation reports, harvesting and citation
out_of_scope: Field-level semantics, datatypes, code lists and contract enforcement (WM-DAT-004 schema / data contract)
The full lineage graph across processing steps and systems (WM-DAT-006 lineage)
The quality rule engine, metric definitions and assessment runs (WM-DAT-007 data quality)
The commercial or consumer-facing offering, SLA and pricing (WM-DAT-008 data product)
Organization and agent master data for holders, publishers and operators (organization model)
Identifier scheme governance and allocation rules (identifier / naming model)
Statistical production semantics such as estimation, weighting and disclosure methodology (official statistics model)
Model training runs and evaluation results that consume the dataset (WM-AI-006)
Study design, protocol and ethics approval of the producing research activity (WM-ACT-036)
Physical storage, indexing and query engines; file systems and databases as such

boundary_notes.distinction: This model records only that a dataset declares conformance to a schema or contract, mirroring dcterms:conformsTo and dcat:Distribution/dcterms:conformsTo. The schema's internal structure, field semantics and enforcement live in WM-DAT-004; duplicating them here would create two masters for one contract.

The dataset carries an asset-level derivation summary (prov:wasDerivedFrom, dcterms:source, schema.org isBasedOn) sufficient for catalogue use. The full activity-entity-agent graph, including intermediate entities and qualified derivations, is composed in from WM-DAT-006.

DQV separates the measurement (attached to the dataset) from the metric and dimension definitions. This model holds the attached measurement, certificate or annotation; metric and dimension definitions and the assessment machinery are owned by WM-DAT-007.

A data product is an offering with consumers, terms and service levels; a dataset is the catalogued asset. DCAT's DataService is the serving surface referenced here, but product packaging, pricing and consumer contracts stay in WM-DAT-008.

DCAT 3 distinguishes the resource from the catalogue record about it. This model keeps the registration facet as a finding on the dataset entry rather than modelling the catalogue itself as an entity; a catalogue with its own governance is a separate registry model.

Training-time selection, splits used and evaluation outcomes belong to the run. The dataset holds only durable ML-readiness documentation such as Croissant RecordSets and RAI statements that remain true independent of any run.
Holder, publisher, creator and contact point are references to agents governed elsewhere; only the role assignment and accountability statement is local to the dataset.

sources.title: Data Catalog Vocabulary (DCAT) - Version 3
sources.relevance: Normative backbone for Catalog, CatalogRecord, Dataset, Distribution, DataService and DatasetSeries, plus checksum, versioning (dcat:version, previousVersion, hasCurrentVersion, versionNotes) and inSeries.

sources.title: Data Quality Vocabulary (DQV)
sources.relevance: Defines QualityMeasurement, Metric, Dimension, Category, QualityAnnotation, QualityCertificate, UserQualityFeedback and QualityPolicy, and their attachment to DCAT datasets and distributions. Note: a WG Note, not a Recommendation.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Entity/Activity/Agent, wasGeneratedBy, wasDerivedFrom, wasAttributedTo, used, generatedAtTime, startedAtTime/endedAtTime and the qualified Derivation/Revision pattern used for asset-level lineage and for event-versus-observation time.

sources.title: DCAT Application Profile for data portals in Europe (DCAT-AP) 3.0.0
sources.relevance: Mandatory/recommended/optional obligations per class, mandated controlled vocabularies (EU data themes, file types, frequency, languages, access rights PUBLIC/RESTRICTED/NON_PUBLIC, ADMS status) and SHACL-based validation of profile conformance.

sources.title: Croissant Format Specification 1.0
sources.relevance: ML-facing dataset description: FileObject, FileSet, RecordSet, Field, DataType, source/extract/transform, SHA-256 on file objects, required conformsTo and SPDX licence guidance, plus the Croissant RAI extension for lifecycle, labelling, uses and limitations.

sources.title: DataCite Metadata Schema 4.6
sources.relevance: Persistent-identifier-centred metadata: Identifier, Creator, Title, Publisher, PublicationYear, ResourceType, Dates/dateTypes, RelatedIdentifier with relationType, Version, Rights, GeoLocation, FundingReference and RelatedItem.

sources.title: Data Package standard (v2)
sources.relevance: Container-level descriptor semantics: required resources array, recommended name/id/licenses/profile, version, created, sources, contributors, and resource-level path/data, encoding, mediatype, bytes and hash.

sources.title: DCAT-US Schema (Project Open Data metadata schema)
sources.version_or_date: DCAT-US v1.1 (6 November 2014); v3.0 published as latest on the same site
sources.relevance: US federal profile requiring title, description, keyword, modified, publisher, contactPoint, identifier, accessLevel, bureauCode, programCode and distribution; evidence that access level and organisational codes are jurisdiction-specific extensions, not universal.

sources.title: RO-Crate 1.2 Specification
sources.relevance: Packaging pattern: ro-crate-metadata.json descriptor, Root Data Entity with conformsTo/identifier/datePublished/license/author, data versus contextual entities, provenance and web-based or detached crates.

sources.title: FAIR Principles
sources.organization: GO FAIR International Support and Coordination Office
sources.version_or_date: Principles as published in Wilkinson et al., Scientific Data, 2016
sources.relevance: F1 globally unique persistent identifier, F3 metadata state the data identifier, A1 retrievable by identifier over a standard protocol, A2 metadata remain accessible when data are gone, I3 qualified references, R1.1 clear usage licence, R1.2 detailed provenance, R1.3 community standards.

sources.title: schema.org type: Dataset
sources.relevance: Web-discovery projection with distribution, includedInDataCatalog, variableMeasured, measurementTechnique, temporalCoverage, spatialCoverage, isBasedOn, version, sdPublisher/sdDatePublished, and an explicit equivalence to dcat:Dataset.

sources.title: RFC 3339: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Normative timestamp profile: full-date and full-time with seconds, mandatory time-offset (Z or numeric), leap-second handling, and the explicit rejection of unqualified local time.

sources.title: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/138 laying down a list of specific high-value datasets and the arrangements for their publication and re-use
sources.version_or_date: Adopted 21 December 2022; OJ L 19, 20.1.2023; applicable from 9 June 2024
sources.relevance: Binding arrangements for designated public-sector datasets: free of charge, machine-readable format, API and bulk download, open licence, and metadata description over six thematic categories under Directive (EU) 2019/1024. Full text retrieval timed out; title, date and obligations confirmed from the EUR-Lex-indexed OJ record.

sources.title: European quality standards / Quality Assurance Framework of the European Statistical System
sources.version_or_date: ESS QAF v1.2; European Statistics Code of Practice; Regulation (EC) 223/2009
sources.relevance: Named output quality dimensions - relevance, accuracy and reliability, timeliness and punctuality, coherence and comparability, accessibility and clarity - used as an authoritative dimension vocabulary alternative to paywalled ISO/IEC 25012.

sources.title: ODRL Information Model 2.2
sources.relevance: Machine-readable rights: Policy (Set/Offer/Agreement), Permission, Prohibition, Duty, Asset, Party, Action, Constraint and the hasPolicy attachment used for use restrictions beyond a licence URL.

sources.title: The Open Archives Initiative Protocol for Metadata Harvesting, Version 2.0
sources.relevance: Federation semantics: item/record/identifier/datestamp/set/metadataPrefix, selective harvesting by from/until datestamps, declared deleted-record support (no/persistent/transient) and mandatory oai_dc.

sources.title: Tombstone Pages (DataCite Support)
sources.relevance: Withdrawal practice: a DataCite DOI cannot be deleted; unavailable content gets a tombstone with full citation, machine-readable DOI and a statement of unavailability, with the DOI moved to the Registered state.

sources.title: Article 10: Data and Data Governance, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act)
sources.organization: EU Artificial Intelligence Act explorer (Future of Life Institute)
sources.version_or_date: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689; Article 10; high-risk obligations applying from 2 August 2026
sources.relevance: Requirements on training, validation and testing data sets: documented design choices, collection origin, preparation operations, assumptions, suitability, bias examination and mitigation, gaps, and relevance/representativeness/error-freeness/completeness. Secondary rendering of the OJ text; verify against EUR-Lex before claiming compliance.

sources.title: DDI-Codebook (DDI-C)
sources.relevance: Study-level documentation of content, meaning, provenance and access for a single dataset, including universe/unit of analysis, sampling, collection period and mode, plus variable-level sources, derivation and access restrictions.

sources.title: Data Catalog Vocabulary (DCAT) - Version 3
sources.relevance: Published by the W3C Dataset Exchange Working Group. Core vocabulary for Dataset, Distribution, DataService, Catalog, CatalogRecord and DatasetSeries, plus version properties, checksum and coverage terms used throughout this model.

sources.title: Data on the Web Best Practices: Data Quality Vocabulary
sources.relevance: Published by the W3C Data on the Web Best Practices Working Group. Supplies quality measurement, metric, dimension, certificate and feedback terms attached to catalogued datasets and distributions.

sources.title: DataCite Metadata Schema Documentation for the Publication and Citation of Research Data and Other Research Outputs
sources.relevance: Maintained by the DataCite Metadata Working Group. Mandatory citation properties, DOI identity, alternate identifiers, date types including Withdrawn, relation types and GeoLocation.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Published by the W3C Provenance Working Group. Generation, derivation, attribution, revision and invalidation terms reused by DCAT and by the lineage sibling model.

sources.title: ISO 19115-1:2014 Geographic information — Metadata — Part 1: Fundamentals
sources.relevance: Published by ISO/TC 211. Geographic metadata fundamentals: scope codes, extent, constraint and lineage packages aligned here without duplication.

sources.title: ISO 19115-1 Metadata Best Practice Guide
sources.organization: Intergovernmental Committee on Surveying and Mapping (Australia / New Zealand)
sources.version_or_date: Guidance compiled for ISO 19115-1:2014 including Amd.1:2018; page dated 2021-09-18
sources.relevance: Compiled by the ICSM Metadata Working Group. Public best-practice guidance used to align ISO 19115-1 constraint, lineage and extent practice where the ISO text is paywalled.

bundles.name: Identity and registration
bundles.description: What this dataset is, how it is named and identified, how its catalogue entry is registered and how it is classified for discovery.
bundles.rationale: DCAT 3 separates the resource from the CatalogRecord that registers it, and FAIR F1/F3 require a globally unique persistent identifier that metadata explicitly bind to the data. Identity and registration must therefore be settled before any other statement about the asset can be trusted.

layers.name: Designation and identity
layers.description: Identifiers, titles, descriptions and languages that make the dataset referable and comprehensible.

findings.name: Dataset identity and designation
findings.description: The identifier set and human designation of the dataset: the authoritative internal identifier held by the master system, any governed persistent identifier such as a DOI or resolvable IRI, alternate identifiers, and multilingual title/description that name the asset for humans.

questions.text: Which system is the master for this dataset's identifier, and what is the identifier it assigns?
Does a governed persistent identifier (DOI, Handle, ARK, resolvable IRI) exist, who registered it, and what does it resolve to?
Does the identifier denote the abstract dataset or one specific version of it?
Which alternate or legacy identifiers must be kept resolvable to avoid breaking existing references?
What title, description and language variants are authoritative for this dataset?

data_elements.name: Master-system dataset identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier assigned by the system of record that owns the dataset entry.

data_elements.name: Persistent identifier
data_elements.description: Governed global identifier such as a DOI or resolvable IRI, with its scheme.

data_elements.name: Title (language-tagged)
data_elements.description: Human-readable name, repeatable per language.

data_elements.name: Description
data_elements.description: Free-text account of the dataset, repeatable per language.

artifacts.name: Dataset metadata record
artifacts.description: The canonical descriptive record for the dataset, serialisable as DCAT/DCAT-AP RDF, DataCite XML/JSON, schema.org JSON-LD or Croissant JSON-LD without changing its semantics.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by the master-system dataset identifier; carries the persistent identifier as an alternate key.

layers.name: Registration and classification
layers.description: The catalogue record that lists the dataset and the controlled terms that make it findable.

findings.name: Catalogue record and listing state
findings.description: The registration facet: which catalogue lists the dataset, when the record was created and modified, the record's own state (draft, listed, hidden, deleted) and the fact that record metadata changes independently of the dataset.

questions.text: In which catalogue or register is this dataset listed, and under what record identifier?
What is the current listing state of the record, and who may change it?
How do record creation and modification times differ from the dataset's own issued and modified times?
Is the same dataset listed in more than one catalogue, and which listing is authoritative?

data_elements.name: Catalogue reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the catalogue or register holding the listing.

data_elements.name: Record listing state
data_elements.description: Registration state of the catalogue record, distinct from the dataset lifecycle state.

data_elements.name: Record created and modified timestamps
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 timestamps for the record itself, used for selective harvesting.

artifacts.name: Catalogue record
artifacts.description: The registration object about the dataset (dcat:CatalogRecord), separable from the dataset metadata record and independently timestamped for harvest.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Catalogue-scoped record identifier plus the referenced dataset identifier.

findings.name: Thematic classification and keywords
findings.description: Controlled-vocabulary themes, keywords, resource type and any mandated classification codes that place the dataset in a discovery taxonomy.

questions.text: Which controlled vocabularies are mandatory for themes in the governing profile, and which terms apply?
What general resource type best describes this asset, and does the target profile constrain the allowed values?
Which free-text keywords are maintained, in which languages, and who curates them?
Is the dataset designated under a regulatory category such as an EU high-value dataset thematic category?

data_elements.name: Theme terms
data_elements.description: URIs from a mandated theme vocabulary.

data_elements.name: Keywords
data_elements.description: Language-tagged free-text tags for discovery.

data_elements.name: Regulatory designation
data_elements.description: Category assigned by a legal instrument, e.g. an HVD thematic category.

artifacts.name: Classification term set
artifacts.description: The resolved set of vocabulary terms bound to the dataset, each with vocabulary URI and version so drift in the source vocabulary is detectable.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Dataset identifier plus vocabulary URI plus term URI.

bundles.name: Scope and structure
bundles.description: What the dataset covers - population, time, space - and what shape it has, including its schema declaration and its membership in a series.
bundles.rationale: Coverage and declared structure are the properties a consumer needs before deciding relevance; DCAT and DCAT-AP carry temporal, spatial and resolution properties, DDI carries universe and unit of analysis, and Croissant and Data Package carry record structure.

layers.name: Coverage
layers.description: The observational, temporal and spatial extent and granularity of the data.

findings.name: Observation unit and granularity
findings.description: The population or universe covered, the unit of observation or analysis, the variables measured, and the resolution at which records are expressed.

questions.text: What population or universe does the dataset claim to cover, and is coverage a census, a sample or opportunistic?
What is the unit of observation of one record, and does it differ from the unit of analysis?
Which variables are measured, and by what measurement technique?
What spatial and temporal resolution do the records carry, and what is the smallest reportable granularity?

data_elements.name: Universe statement
data_elements.description: Description of the population the data is intended to represent.

data_elements.name: Unit of observation
data_elements.description: The entity type that one record describes.

data_elements.name: Temporal resolution
data_elements.description: Minimum time period resolvable in the data.

data_elements.name: Record count
data_elements.description: Number of records or observations at a stated point in time.

artifacts.name: Coverage statement
artifacts.description: A structured statement of universe, unit, variables and resolution, suitable for publication as a codebook section or as Croissant RecordSet documentation.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Dataset identifier plus version identifier, since coverage changes between versions.

findings.name: Temporal coverage and currency
findings.description: The period the data describes, the reference date of the content, and the currency of the asset expressed through issued, modified and next-expected-update times.

questions.text: What start and end instants does the data content cover, and is the interval open-ended?
What is the reference date of the content, as distinct from the date the metadata was recorded?
When was the dataset last updated and when is the next update expected?
Which time zone or offset applies to the timestamps inside the data, and is it recorded explicitly?

data_elements.name: Temporal coverage interval
data_elements.description: Start and end of the period described by the data, as RFC 3339 timestamps or dates.

data_elements.name: Issued and modified timestamps
data_elements.description: Release and last-change times of the dataset itself.

data_elements.name: Next expected update
data_elements.description: Planned next release instant, where a cadence is declared.

artifacts.name: Temporal coverage record
artifacts.description: Machine-readable interval and currency block covering content period, issue, modification and expected update.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Dataset version identifier plus interval bounds.

findings.name: Spatial coverage and reference system
findings.description: Geographic extent, named places, coordinate reference system and spatial resolution, applicable when the data has a location dimension.

questions.text: What geographic extent does the dataset cover, expressed as named places, codes or a bounding geometry?
Which coordinate reference system do the coordinates use, and is it stated by registry identifier?
What is the spatial resolution or smallest geographic unit released, and does disclosure control coarsen it?
If the dataset has no spatial dimension, is that recorded explicitly rather than left empty?

data_elements.name: Spatial extent
data_elements.description: Named place references or bounding geometry for the covered area.

data_elements.name: Coordinate reference system identifier
data_elements.description: Registry identifier of the CRS used by coordinates in the data.

data_elements.name: Spatial resolution
data_elements.description: Resolution in metres or as an equivalent unit statement.

artifacts.name: Spatial extent record
artifacts.description: Geometry or place-code block with an explicit CRS reference, publishable in a geospatial metadata profile.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Dataset version identifier plus geometry hash or place-code set.

layers.name: Structure and membership
layers.description: The declared schema the data claims to follow and the dataset's place in a series or aggregate.

findings.name: Declared schema reference
findings.description: The reference from the dataset to the schema, data dictionary or data contract it conforms to, with the version of that schema and whether conformance is asserted or verified.

questions.text: Which schema, profile or data contract does the dataset declare conformance to, and at which version?
Is conformance asserted by the publisher or verified by a validator, and where is the evidence?
Where is the field-level data dictionary published, and does it cover code lists and missing-value conventions?
How is divergence between the declared schema and the served data detected and reported?

data_elements.name: Conforms-to reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the schema or standard the data claims to follow.

data_elements.name: Declared schema version
data_elements.description: Version string of the referenced schema at time of declaration.

data_elements.name: Conformance status
data_elements.description: Whether conformance is asserted, verified or failing.

artifacts.name: Schema declaration
artifacts.description: The binding between the dataset (or a distribution) and an external schema artefact, holding the reference, version and conformance status only.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Dataset version identifier plus schema reference plus schema version.

findings.name: Series and aggregate membership
findings.description: Whether the dataset is an edition or slice of a continuing series, part of a larger aggregate, or a standalone asset, and the ordering relations among members.

questions.text: Is this dataset a member of a dataset series, and what identifies the series?
Which member precedes and follows this one, and on what ordering property?
Is a new release a new series member or a new version of the same dataset, and which rule decides?
Does the dataset aggregate identifiable parts or subsets that are themselves catalogued?

data_elements.name: Series membership reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the dataset series this dataset belongs to.

data_elements.name: Member ordering key
data_elements.description: Ordering value, usually the coverage period start, used to sequence members.

data_elements.name: Part references
data_elements.description: References to catalogued subsets or components.

artifacts.name: Series membership record
artifacts.description: Edge record binding a dataset to a series with ordering and role, kept separate so the series can be governed by its own holder.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Series identifier plus member dataset identifier; ordering key carried as an attribute, never as the identifier.

bundles.name: Representation and access
bundles.description: How the dataset is materialised as distributions and served through endpoints, and under what access conditions.
bundles.rationale: DCAT separates the abstract dataset from Distributions and DataServices; FAIR A1 requires retrieval by identifier over a standardised protocol; EU high-value dataset rules make API and bulk download availability a legal obligation for designated data.

layers.name: Distributions and packaging
layers.description: Concrete serialisations of the dataset with format, size, fixity and packaging conventions.

findings.name: Distribution manifest and fixity
findings.description: Each accessible form of the dataset - its media type and format, byte size, download and access URLs, compression or packaging profile, and the checksum that lets a consumer verify the bytes received.

questions.text: Which distributions exist for this dataset, and what media type and format does each use?
What checksum algorithm and value is published for each distribution, and when was fixity last verified?
Is the distribution packaged in a container profile such as a data package or research object crate, and where is its descriptor?
Are the distributions semantically equivalent renderings of the same content, or do some carry reduced or transformed content?
What byte size and record volume should a consumer plan for, and how volatile is that size?

data_elements.name: Media type
data_elements.description: IANA media type of the distribution.

data_elements.name: Byte size
data_elements.description: Size of the distribution in bytes at a stated time.

data_elements.name: Checksum
data_elements.description: Algorithm and digest value for byte-level integrity verification.

data_elements.name: Download URL
data_elements.description: Direct retrieval URL for the distribution's bytes.

data_elements.name: Packaging profile
data_elements.description: Container convention the distribution follows, with its descriptor location.

artifacts.name: Distribution
artifacts.description: An accessible form of the dataset: file, archive, package or dump, described by a manifest entry with format, size, fixity and access URLs.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Dataset version identifier plus distribution identifier assigned by the master system; checksum used for content-equality checks, never as the primary key.

layers.name: Access channels and conditions
layers.description: Services that serve the data and the conditions under which access is granted.

findings.name: Access service and protocol
findings.description: Endpoints that serve the dataset - APIs, query services, streams or bulk download points - with their protocol, declared conformance class, documentation and operational limits.

questions.text: Which services serve this dataset, and what is the endpoint URL and description of each?
What protocol or API standard does each endpoint implement, and which conformance classes does it declare?
What rate limits, pagination, quota or payload limits apply to programmatic access?
Is a bulk download path available alongside the API, as required for designated public-sector datasets?

data_elements.name: Endpoint URL
data_elements.description: Root URL of the service serving the dataset.

data_elements.name: Protocol or API standard
data_elements.description: Identifier of the protocol the endpoint implements.

data_elements.name: Service limits
data_elements.description: Declared operational limits such as rate, quota and page size.

artifacts.name: Access service descriptor
artifacts.description: Machine-readable description of the serving endpoint, including protocol, conformance and documentation links; the API definition document itself is referenced, not owned here.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Service identifier from the master system plus endpoint URL as an alternate key.

findings.name: Access conditions and embargo
findings.description: The access level of the asset, authentication and authorisation requirements, request and approval processes for restricted data, and time-bound embargoes.

questions.text: What is the declared access level of this dataset, using the governing profile's vocabulary?
What authentication and authorisation does each channel require, and who can approve a grant?
If access is restricted, what is the request process, expected decision time and appeal route?
Is an embargo in force, when does it lift, and what becomes available at that moment?
When the data itself is restricted, does descriptive metadata remain publicly visible?

data_elements.name: Access rights code
data_elements.description: Coded access level such as public, restricted or non-public.

data_elements.name: Authentication requirement
data_elements.description: Method required to authenticate before access is granted.

data_elements.name: Embargo end
data_elements.description: Instant at which restricted status is scheduled to lapse.

artifacts.name: Access condition statement
artifacts.description: Human- and machine-readable statement of access level, conditions and request route, publishable on a landing page even when the data is closed.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Dataset identifier plus condition statement identifier and effective-from timestamp as an attribute.

bundles.name: Rights and accountability
bundles.description: Who is accountable for the dataset, under what licence and restrictions it may be used, and what protections apply to personal or sensitive content.
bundles.rationale: FAIR R1.1 requires a clear usage licence and R1.2 detailed provenance; DCAT-AP mandates publisher and licence vocabularies; ODRL provides machine-readable permissions, prohibitions and duties beyond a single licence URL; AI Act Article 10 adds documented governance duties for training data.

layers.name: Rights and licensing
layers.description: Licence, rights holder and machine-readable use restrictions.

findings.name: Licence and rights statement
findings.description: The licence under which each distribution is offered, expressed by a governed licence identifier, together with the rights holder, attribution requirement and any separate rights statement for metadata versus data.

questions.text: Which licence applies to each distribution, identified by a governed licence identifier rather than free text?
Who holds the rights being licensed, and on what basis do they hold them?
What attribution text or citation must a re-user reproduce?
Does the metadata carry a different licence from the data itself?
Does a legal obligation constrain the licence choice, such as an open licence mandate for designated datasets?

data_elements.name: Licence identifier
data_elements.description: Governed identifier of the licence, e.g. an SPDX identifier or an authority-list URI.

data_elements.name: Rights holder
data_elements.description: Reference to the agent holding the rights being licensed.

data_elements.name: Attribution statement
data_elements.description: Text a re-user must reproduce to satisfy the licence.

artifacts.name: Licence binding
artifacts.description: Record binding a distribution or the dataset to a licence identifier, rights holder and attribution text, with its own effective period so licence changes are auditable.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Distribution or dataset identifier plus licence identifier plus a monotonic binding sequence number.

findings.name: Use restrictions and machine-readable policy
findings.description: Permissions, prohibitions and duties that a licence alone does not express: third-party rights, contractual limits, purpose limitations, redistribution and text-and-data-mining conditions.

questions.text: Which actions are permitted, prohibited or subject to a duty, and for which assignee parties?
Do third-party rights encumber part of the content, and which part?
Are there purpose limitations, such as research-only use or a prohibition on training models?
Is the policy expressed in a machine-readable form an agent can evaluate before use?

data_elements.name: Policy reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a machine-readable policy governing use of the asset.

data_elements.name: Prohibited actions
data_elements.description: Actions the policy forbids on the asset.

data_elements.name: Purpose limitation
data_elements.description: Declared limitation on the purposes for which the data may be used.

artifacts.name: Use policy
artifacts.description: Machine-readable policy set attaching permissions, prohibitions, duties and constraints to the dataset as an asset.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Policy identifier from the issuing authority plus asset reference; versioned rather than overwritten.

layers.name: Accountability and protection
layers.description: Named roles accountable for the asset and the controls applied to personal or otherwise sensitive content.

findings.name: Holder, publisher and contact roles
findings.description: The accountable data holder, the publisher that lists the dataset, creators or contributors, and the contact point through which questions and access requests are handled.

questions.text: Which party is accountable for the content and service level of this dataset?
How do the holder, publisher, creator and catalogue operator differ for this asset, and are any the same party?
What contact point is published, and is it a durable role address rather than an individual?
Who is the operational steward responsible for updates, quality checks and metadata upkeep?

data_elements.name: Holder reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the accountable party for the asset.

data_elements.name: Publisher reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the party making the dataset available.

data_elements.name: Contact point
data_elements.description: Published contact channel for the dataset.

artifacts.name: Role assignment record
artifacts.description: Edge record binding a party reference to a role on the dataset with an effective period, so accountability history survives party changes.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Dataset identifier plus role code plus party identifier plus assignment sequence.

findings.name: Personal and sensitive data controls
findings.description: Whether the dataset contains personal, confidential or otherwise sensitive content, what legal basis and protective measures apply, and what disclosure control has been performed.

questions.text: Does the dataset contain personal or otherwise sensitive data, and which components carry it?
On what legal basis or consent is the sensitive content processed and published?
What de-identification or statistical disclosure control has been applied, and with what residual risk?
Could this dataset be combined with others to re-identify individuals, and is that risk documented?
If special-category data is retained solely for bias detection, are the required safeguards documented?

data_elements.name: Sensitivity classification
data_elements.description: Coded classification of the sensitivity of the dataset content.

data_elements.name: De-identification method
data_elements.description: Method applied to reduce identifiability, with the time it was applied.

data_elements.name: Legal basis
data_elements.description: Cited basis on which sensitive content is processed and released.

artifacts.name: Sensitivity assessment
artifacts.description: Dated assessment recording sensitivity classification, applied controls, residual risk and reviewer, retained even after the dataset is withdrawn.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Dataset version identifier plus assessment identifier; supersession recorded by reference to the prior assessment.

bundles.name: Lifecycle and provenance
bundles.description: Where the dataset came from, how it changes over time, and how it is retired, preserved or deleted.
bundles.rationale: PROV-O supplies the derivation and attribution model, DCAT 3 the version chain, OAI-PMH the deleted-record semantics for federated consumers, DataCite the tombstone practice, and FAIR A2 the requirement that metadata outlive the data.

layers.name: Provenance
layers.description: Origin, derivation and production method at asset level.

findings.name: Source and derivation
findings.description: The upstream datasets, systems or collection activities this dataset was derived from, the agent responsible, and the generation event that produced this version.

questions.text: Which upstream datasets or sources was this dataset derived from, and at which of their versions?
Which activity generated this version, when did it start and end, and which agent was responsible?
To whom is the dataset attributed, as distinct from who published it?
How far back does asset-level lineage go here before the question is delegated to the lineage model?

data_elements.name: Derived-from reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an upstream dataset or entity this dataset was derived from.

data_elements.name: Generated-by activity reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the activity that produced this dataset version.

data_elements.name: Generated-at time
data_elements.description: Instant at which this version came into existence, distinct from when it was catalogued.

artifacts.name: Provenance record
artifacts.description: Asset-level provenance bundle linking this dataset version to sources, generating activity and responsible agents, exportable as a PROV graph.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Dataset version identifier plus provenance bundle identifier assigned by the recording system.

findings.name: Production method and processing
findings.description: How the data was collected or computed: collection mode, instruments, sampling procedure, processing and cleaning steps, and the assumptions those steps embed.

questions.text: By what mode and instrument was the data collected or generated?
Which preparation operations - cleaning, joining, labelling, aggregation - were applied, and in what order?
What assumptions or design choices does the production method embed that a re-user must know?
Can the production be re-executed, and what would be needed to reproduce this exact output?

data_elements.name: Collection mode
data_elements.description: Coded mode by which the underlying observations were obtained.

data_elements.name: Processing steps
data_elements.description: Ordered summary of preparation operations applied to produce this version.

data_elements.name: Method assumptions
data_elements.description: Stated assumptions embedded by the production method.

artifacts.name: Method documentation
artifacts.description: Methodology description covering collection, sampling and processing, published alongside the dataset as a codebook or datasheet section.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Dataset version identifier plus document identifier; superseded documents retained by reference.

layers.name: Versioning and release
layers.description: Version identity, change records and the cadence and status of releases.

findings.name: Version identity and change record
findings.description: How versions are identified and chained, what changed between them, whether a change is breaking, and which version is current.

questions.text: What versioning scheme is used, and does a new version get a new persistent identifier?
Which version precedes this one, which supersedes it, and which is currently authoritative?
What changed relative to the previous version, and is the change breaking for consumers?
Which event triggers a new version rather than an in-place correction?

data_elements.name: Version string
data_elements.description: Version label of this dataset edition.

data_elements.name: Previous version reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the immediately preceding version.

data_elements.name: Version notes
data_elements.description: Description of the changes introduced by this version.

data_elements.name: Breaking change flag
data_elements.description: Whether the change requires consumer action.

artifacts.name: Change log entry
artifacts.description: Per-version entry recording what changed, when it was released and whether it breaks consumers; the change log is the append-only series of these entries.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Dataset identifier plus version identifier plus monotonic entry sequence; dates are attributes, never the key.

findings.name: Release cadence and status
findings.description: The declared update frequency, planned release calendar, punctuality against that plan, and the maturity or availability status of the asset.

questions.text: What update frequency is declared, using which controlled vocabulary?
How does actual release timing compare with the announced calendar?
What is the current status of the asset - draft, in development, stable, deprecated - and who sets it?
Is any part served in real time or near real time, and what latency is guaranteed?

data_elements.name: Accrual frequency
data_elements.description: Coded frequency at which the dataset is updated.

data_elements.name: Status code
data_elements.description: Maturity or availability status of the dataset or distribution.

data_elements.name: Planned release instant
data_elements.description: Announced instant of a future release.

artifacts.name: Release calendar
artifacts.description: Published schedule of planned releases with announced and actual instants, enabling punctuality measurement.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Dataset identifier plus calendar entry identifier; announced instant stored as an attribute of the entry.

layers.name: Retirement and retention
layers.description: Deprecation, withdrawal, tombstoning, retention scheduling and deletion.

findings.name: Deprecation and withdrawal
findings.description: How a dataset is marked superseded or removed from service, what replaces it, what consumers are told, and what remains resolvable after removal.

questions.text: Is the dataset deprecated or withdrawn, when did that take effect and on whose decision?
What supersedes the withdrawn dataset, and how are consumers redirected?
What does the tombstone record state, and does it keep the citation and identifier resolvable?
How is removal signalled to downstream catalogues that previously harvested this record?

data_elements.name: Retirement state
data_elements.description: Coded retirement state such as active, deprecated or withdrawn.

data_elements.name: Successor reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the dataset that replaces this one.

data_elements.name: Tombstone URL
data_elements.description: Location of the page stating why the asset is unavailable.

artifacts.name: Tombstone record
artifacts.description: Persisting record containing the full citation, the identifier in human- and machine-readable form and a statement of unavailability; it survives deletion of the payload.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Persistent identifier of the withdrawn dataset, retained and never reassigned.

findings.name: Retention, preservation and deletion
findings.description: The retention rule governing how long the dataset and its distributions are kept, the preservation commitment, and how deletion is executed and evidenced without destroying the descriptive record.

questions.text: Which retention rule applies, what is the retention period and what triggers its start?
What preservation commitment has the holder made, and for which distributions?
When data is deleted, what is deleted, what metadata is retained, and where is the deletion evidenced?
How are conflicts resolved between an erasure obligation and an archival or legal-hold obligation?

data_elements.name: Retention rule reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the governing retention schedule or policy.

data_elements.name: Retain-until instant
data_elements.description: Computed instant until which the asset must be kept.

data_elements.name: Legal hold flag
data_elements.description: Whether deletion is suspended by a hold.

artifacts.name: Retention schedule entry
artifacts.description: Binding of the dataset to a retention rule with computed retain-until instant, hold status and executed-deletion evidence.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Dataset identifier plus retention rule identifier plus entry sequence.

bundles.name: Quality and fitness
bundles.description: Measured quality attached to the asset and the judgement of whether it is fit for a stated purpose, including AI training use.
bundles.rationale: DQV attaches measurements, annotations and certificates to DCAT datasets while keeping metric definitions separate; the ESS quality framework supplies an authoritative dimension vocabulary; AI Act Article 10 and the Croissant RAI extension make documented limitations a requirement for training data rather than a courtesy.

layers.name: Quality measurement
layers.description: Measured quality results attached to the dataset or its distributions.

findings.name: Quality measurements
findings.description: Individual measurements of a quality metric computed on this dataset or distribution, each with its value, metric reference, dimension, method and measurement time, plus certificates or user feedback where they exist.

questions.text: Which metric was computed, in which quality dimension, and what value resulted?
What exactly was measured - the whole dataset, one distribution, or a subset?
When was the measurement computed, and against which dataset version?
What threshold makes the result acceptable, and who set it?
Do certificates or user feedback annotations exist alongside computed measurements?

data_elements.name: Metric reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the metric definition governed by the quality model.

data_elements.name: Measured value
data_elements.description: Result of computing the metric on the target.

data_elements.name: Measured-at timestamp
data_elements.description: Instant at which the measurement was computed.

data_elements.name: Quality dimension
data_elements.description: Dimension the metric belongs to, e.g. accuracy, timeliness, coherence.

artifacts.name: Quality measurement record
artifacts.description: Immutable record of one metric computation against a stated target and version, retained as an evidence series.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Target reference plus metric reference plus measurement sequence assigned by the measuring system; the measurement time is an attribute.

layers.name: Fitness and limitations
layers.description: Judgements about suitability for stated purposes and documented limitations, including AI-specific readiness.

findings.name: Fitness for use and known limitations
findings.description: Statements of intended and discouraged uses, known caveats, coverage gaps, comparability breaks, and who made the fitness judgement for which purpose.

questions.text: For which stated purpose has fitness been assessed, and what was the verdict?
What known limitations, caveats or coverage gaps must a re-user account for?
Which uses are explicitly discouraged or unsupported by the holder?
Are there breaks in series or definitional changes that prevent comparison across time or units?

data_elements.name: Intended use statement
data_elements.description: Purpose for which the holder considers the dataset suitable.

data_elements.name: Limitation statement
data_elements.description: Documented caveat, gap or defect affecting reuse.

data_elements.name: Fitness verdict
data_elements.description: Coded outcome of a fitness assessment for a stated purpose.

artifacts.name: Fitness assessment
artifacts.description: Dated assessment binding a purpose to a verdict with supporting limitations and evidence references; commonly published as a datasheet or quality report section.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Dataset version identifier plus purpose identifier plus assessment sequence.

findings.name: ML readiness and training use
findings.description: The durable documentation an ML consumer needs: record structure and field typing, label provenance and annotation process, representativeness and bias examination, and any restriction on using the dataset to train models.

questions.text: Is the dataset described in a machine-readable ML format that resolves files to record sets and typed fields?
How were labels or annotations produced, by whom, and with what agreement or review?
What is documented about representativeness relative to the target population and about examined biases?
Is training a model on this dataset permitted, restricted or prohibited, and by which instrument?
Are canonical splits or benchmark subsets defined at asset level, or left to the consuming training run?

data_elements.name: ML description reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a machine-readable ML dataset description document.

data_elements.name: Annotation process description
data_elements.description: How labels were produced and reviewed.

data_elements.name: Bias examination result
data_elements.description: Outcome of examining the data for biases affecting people or outcomes.

data_elements.name: Training permission
data_elements.description: Whether model training on the dataset is permitted.

artifacts.name: ML dataset description
artifacts.description: Machine-readable description resolving distributions to record sets, fields and types, with responsible-AI statements attached; loadable by ML frameworks without bespoke code.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Dataset version identifier plus description document identifier and declared conformsTo version.

bundles.name: Interoperability and exchange
bundles.description: How the dataset entry conforms to external profiles, is validated, is exchanged with other catalogues, and is cited and linked.
bundles.rationale: Real catalogues must satisfy jurisdictional profiles, prove conformance by validation, exchange records by harvest, and support citation with typed relations; each of these is specified by a distinct authority and none can be assumed from the others.

layers.name: Profiles and validation
layers.description: Declared application profiles and the validation evidence for them.

findings.name: Application profile conformance and validation
findings.description: Which application profiles the catalogue entry claims to satisfy, the obligations those profiles impose, the validation performed against them, and the mapping losses when projecting into each profile.

questions.text: Which application profiles does this entry declare conformance to, at which versions?
Which properties are mandatory under each declared profile, and are all of them populated?
What validation was run, against which rule set, and what were the violations?
What information is lost or coerced when projecting this entry into a given profile?
Where two declared profiles disagree on a property's obligation or vocabulary, which prevails?

data_elements.name: Profile reference
data_elements.description: Identifier and version of a declared application profile.

data_elements.name: Validation outcome
data_elements.description: Pass, warn or fail result of validating the entry against a profile rule set.

data_elements.name: Violation count
data_elements.description: Number of rule violations found in the latest validation run.

artifacts.name: Validation report
artifacts.description: Machine-readable report of a validation run against a named profile rule set, with per-rule outcomes and timestamps; retained as evidence for conformance claims.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Entry identifier plus rule set identifier plus run sequence assigned by the validator.

layers.name: Exchange and linkage
layers.description: Harvesting between catalogues and typed links to other resources.

findings.name: Harvesting and federation
findings.description: How the entry is exchanged with other catalogues: source of truth, harvest datestamps and increments, deleted-record signalling, duplicate detection and the rules for locally overriding harvested values.

questions.text: Was this entry authored locally or harvested, and from which source catalogue?
Which datestamp drives incremental harvesting, and at what granularity is it exposed?
What deleted-record support does the source declare, and how are removals propagated?
May local edits override harvested values, and how is the divergence recorded and reconciled?
How are duplicate entries for the same dataset across federated catalogues detected and merged?

data_elements.name: Origin code
data_elements.description: Whether the entry is locally authored, harvested or mirrored.

data_elements.name: Source record identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the record in the source catalogue.

data_elements.name: Harvest datestamp
data_elements.description: Datestamp used for selective harvesting of this record.

artifacts.name: Harvest log entry
artifacts.description: Per-run record of what was fetched, changed, deleted or rejected during a harvest, supporting replay and divergence analysis.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Source catalogue identifier plus harvest run sequence; run start time recorded as an attribute.

findings.name: Citation and related identifiers
findings.description: The citation form of the dataset and its typed relations to publications, software, source datasets, successors and other resources.

questions.text: What is the recommended citation for this dataset, and which version does it pin?
Which typed relations to other resources are asserted, using which relation-type vocabulary?
Are related references qualified enough for a machine to know the direction and nature of each link?
Who must be credited in the citation, and how are contributor roles distinguished from creators?

data_elements.name: Citation string
data_elements.description: Recommended human-readable citation for the dataset.

data_elements.name: Related identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of a related resource with its relation type.

data_elements.name: Creator list
data_elements.description: Ordered creators credited for the dataset.

artifacts.name: Citation block
artifacts.description: Structured citation and typed relation set exportable to a citation format or embedded in the metadata record; retained on tombstones after withdrawal.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Dataset version identifier plus persistent identifier; relation entries keyed by related identifier plus relation type.

functions.name: Register dataset
functions.description: Create the dataset entry and its catalogue record, assigning the master-system identifier and, where applicable, requesting a persistent identifier.
preconditions: Holder is resolvable in the organization model
Target application profile is declared
No existing entry matches the identity keys
effects: Dataset identifier is allocated and reserved permanently
Catalogue record created with RFC 3339 creation timestamp

functions.name: Publish distribution
functions.description: Attach an accessible form of the dataset with format, size, access URLs and checksum, and expose it through the declared channels.
preconditions: Dataset entry exists and is not withdrawn
Licence binding exists for the distribution
Access conditions are declared
effects: Distribution becomes discoverable
Fixity baseline is recorded for later verification

functions.name: Verify fixity
functions.description: Recompute the checksum of a distribution and compare it with the published value.
preconditions: Distribution is retrievable
A checksum algorithm and value are published
effects: Mismatch raises an integrity incident and marks the distribution suspect

functions.name: Issue version
functions.description: Create a new dataset version, chain it to its predecessor and record what changed and whether the change is breaking.
preconditions: Versioning rule determines that a new version rather than a correction is required
Predecessor version is identified
effects: Predecessor is no longer current but stays resolvable
Consumers of a pinned version are unaffected

functions.name: Record quality measurement
functions.description: Attach a computed metric result to a stated target and version with its dimension, method and measurement time.
preconditions: Metric is defined in the governing quality model
Target version is identified
effects: Measurement series is appended, never overwritten
Failing thresholds can trigger a fitness re-assessment

functions.name: Validate against profile
functions.description: Run the rule set of a declared application profile against the catalogue entry and record the violations.
preconditions: Profile version is resolvable
Entry is serialisable into the profile's model
effects: Conformance claims become evidence-backed
Failing entries can be blocked from publication or harvest

functions.name: Evaluate access request
functions.description: Decide a request for a restricted dataset against its access conditions and machine-readable policy.
preconditions: Access level is declared
Approver role is assigned
Policy is resolvable
effects: Grant is time-bounded and auditable
Refusals record the reason and appeal route

functions.name: Harvest entry
functions.description: Fetch or refresh a catalogue entry from a source catalogue using selective harvesting and apply local override rules.
preconditions: Source declares its deleted-record support level
Local override policy is defined
effects: Local entries diverge only where policy allows
Deletions propagate to downstream consumers

functions.name: Withdraw dataset
functions.description: Remove a dataset from service, publish a tombstone and notify downstream catalogues while keeping identifiers resolvable.
preconditions: Withdrawal is authorised by the holder
Retention obligations have been checked
effects: Persistent identifier resolves to a tombstone rather than failing
Descriptive metadata survives the payload

functions.name: Execute retention action
functions.description: Apply the retention rule at its trigger point: extend, archive or delete the payload, and record the evidence.
preconditions: Retain-until instant has passed
No legal hold is in force
Approver has authorised the action
effects: Payload is archived or destroyed as ruled
Tombstone and citation metadata are retained

functions.name: Project entry to a target format
functions.description: Render the neutral dataset entry into a target serialisation or profile, recording any lossy mapping.
preconditions: Target profile is declared and versioned
Canonicalisation rules are applied before projection
effects: Projection is reproducible and comparable across runs
Lost fields are disclosed rather than silently dropped

functions.name: Bind data service
functions.description: Attach a data service endpoint that serves the dataset and optionally backs a distribution.
preconditions: endpoint URL is an IRI
service versus payload conformance targets are distinct
effects: service listed
servesDataset and accessService links updated

functions.name: Attach dataset to series
functions.description: Add a separately published dataset to an explicit DatasetSeries and update first, previous and last navigation.
preconditions: series is typed DatasetSeries
member is not being faked as an extra distribution of another member
effects: membership and navigation properties updated

functions.name: Record generation or derivation
functions.description: Point the dataset at generating activities and source entities, composing WM-DAT-006 for the full graph.
preconditions: activity times use RFC 3339 with seconds and offset
effects: wasGeneratedBy and wasDerivedFrom asserted
lineage sibling updated

functions.name: Cite dataset
functions.description: Build a citation from mandatory DataCite-style properties and the chosen persistent identifier.
preconditions: mandatory citation properties present or replaced with DataCite unknown codes
effects: isReferencedBy relations may be added on the dataset

composition.purpose: The dataset declares conformance to a schema or data contract; the schema's field semantics, datatypes and enforcement stay in WM-DAT-004 so there is one master for the contract.
Asset-level derivation here is a projection of the full lineage graph; WM-DAT-006 supplies activities, agents and qualified derivations beyond the immediate sources.

Quality measurements attach to the dataset while metric, dimension and threshold definitions and the assessment machinery are owned by WM-DAT-007, following the DQV split between measurement and metric.
Inbound: a data product catalog entry references one or more datasets. The offering, its consumers and its service levels are not modelled here.
Inbound: a training run references dataset versions it consumed. Split selection and evaluation results belong to the run; only durable ML-readiness documentation is held here.
Inbound: a study produces datasets. The registry records this as PRODUCES; expressed here as a reference because study design, protocol and ethics remain in the study model.

composition.target: Organization / agent model (registry identifier to be confirmed)
composition.purpose: Holder, publisher, creator, contributor and service operator are agent references; only the role assignment and its effective period are local.

composition.target: Identifier and naming scheme model (registry identifier to be confirmed)
composition.purpose: Persistent identifier schemes, allocation authority and resolution policy are governed externally; the dataset records only the identifier value and its scheme.

Primary alignment for Dataset, Distribution, DataService, DatasetSeries and CatalogRecord, and for checksum and version chaining. Alignment, not conformance: profile obligations are validated per deployment.
Jurisdictional profiles that add mandatory properties and controlled vocabularies; recorded as declared profiles with validation evidence rather than as built-in obligations.
Quality measurement facet applied to datasets and distributions, kept as a mix-in so quality can be absent without breaking the entry.
Provenance facet for derivation, attribution and generation time, including the distinction between generation and recording instants.
Extends the catalogue entry with ML-loadable record set structure and responsible-AI documentation for training use.
Citation, persistent identifier, typed related identifiers and tombstone practice for research and repository contexts.
Packaging profiles for distributions, providing descriptor conventions, resource-level integrity and payload-plus-metadata containers.
Exchange semantics for federated catalogues: selective harvesting by datestamp and declared deleted-record support.
Machine-readable permissions, prohibitions and duties where a licence identifier alone cannot express the terms.

owner_package_requirements: A Dimension adopting WM-DAT-001 must name the accountable data holder role and the system of record that mints dataset identifiers before any entry is created.
It must declare which application profiles are binding for its catalogue (for example DCAT-AP or DCAT-US) and pin their versions, because mandatory-property sets differ between them.
It must bind the controlled vocabularies it uses for theme, format, frequency, access rights and licence, and record the vocabulary version so term drift is detectable.
It must state its retention, tombstone and deleted-record policy, including whether harvesters are told about deletions persistently or transiently.
It must declare whether quality metrics come from a shared metric registry (WM-DAT-007) or from local definitions, and record which.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Use a stable namespace of the form <dimension>.dataset with bundle-level segments (identity, scope, representation, rights, lifecycle, quality, interoperability). Local IDs stay lower-kebab-case and never encode dates, jurisdictions or storage technology; jurisdictional specifics belong in profile declarations, not in names.
registry_links: vr.wm-dat-001 is the registry entry for this model; nav path NAV.INF.DAT.SET
Relations are maintained in planning/VERCY-MODEL-RELATIONS.csv, including the inbound PRODUCES edge from WM-ACT-036 which this model expresses as a reference
Profile and vocabulary registries used by a Dimension must be listed with URI and version alongside the model registration

canonicalization_rules: Canonical form is the format-neutral entry: identifiers, typed values and references, with no serialisation artefacts. JSON, YAML, Markdown, RDF, Git and MongoDB are projections.
Timestamps are canonicalised to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset; UTC is written as Z and local offsets are preserved rather than normalised away when the offset carries meaning.
Reference values are canonicalised to the identifier plus scheme, never to a display label; controlled-vocabulary values are canonicalised to term URI plus vocabulary version.
Collections that carry no inherent order (keywords, themes, distributions) are sorted by identifier before hashing so that equality checks are stable.
patch_rules: Patches target one finding at a time and cite the source_refs that justify the change; a patch that adds structure without a source is rejected.
Corrections that do not change data content update the entry in place; changes to content, coverage or structure require a new dataset version and a change log entry.
Withdrawal is a state transition plus a tombstone, never a delete of the entry; identifiers are never reassigned.
Harvested fields may only be patched locally where the override policy allows, and each override records the overridden source value.
compatibility_rules: Adding an optional data element or a new finding is backward compatible; making an element required, narrowing a vocabulary or removing an element is breaking and requires a major model version.
Profile declarations may be added or removed without breaking the entry; failing a newly declared profile is a validation finding, not a model break.
Consumers must tolerate unknown optional elements and must not infer absence of a fact from absence of an element unless a not-applicable flag is present.
A projection may omit elements only if it publishes a loss report; silent narrowing is non-conformant.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier: the identifier assigned by the system of record that owns the dataset entry always takes precedence.
Governed global identifier or IRI: a DOI, Handle, ARK or other registered persistent identifier or resolvable IRI, used when no master-system identifier exists or as the public alternate key.
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension: used only when neither of the above exists, and recorded as locally minted.
Checksums, titles, URLs and version strings are attributes, never primary identifiers; a date or period is never an identifier.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All timestamps use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset (Z for UTC or a numeric offset such as +02:00); unqualified local time is not accepted. Event time and observation or ingestion time are recorded separately whenever they can differ: dataset generation time and coverage period are event times, while catalogue record creation, harvest datestamp, measurement time and validation run time are observation or ingestion times. Where only one is known, the entry states which one it is rather than conflating them.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artefacts (distributions, change log entries, quality measurements, validation reports, harvest log entries, role assignments, licence bindings, retention entries) are named by parent identifier plus a monotonic sequence assigned by the recording system - for example <dataset-id>/<version-id>/measurement/000123. Sequence numbers never encode dates, and gaps are permitted but never reused.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every distribution carries a checksum with a named algorithm; fixity is re-verified on a declared schedule and on every re-publication, and a mismatch marks the distribution suspect rather than silently replacing the published value. Evidence artefacts (measurements, validation reports, assessments, tombstones) are append-only: they are superseded by reference, never edited in place.

policies: A dataset entry is publishable only when it has an identifier, a holder, an access rights code and at least one distribution or a documented reason why none exists.
Conformance to an external standard is claimed only with a stored validation report; a declared profile without evidence is recorded as a claim, not as conformance.
Descriptive metadata outlives the payload: withdrawal or deletion of data never deletes the identifier, citation or tombstone record.
Restricted datasets remain discoverable at metadata level by default; suppression of metadata requires a named exception with an approver and an expiry.
Quality measurements and fitness assessments are always bound to a specific dataset version; unversioned quality claims are rejected.
The data holder is accountable for content and service levels; catalogue operators list and harvest but do not become holders by copying metadata.
Absence of a licence is not a grant; open reuse requires an explicit licence or rights statement on the dataset or distribution.
Multiple distributions of one dataset are not automatically a dataset series; DatasetSeries must be typed explicitly.
Quality statements are assessments by named agents, not intrinsic properties of bytes; conflicting assessments may coexist and are composed from WM-DAT-007.
Persistent identifiers of cited datasets are not recycled; legal erasure suppresses bytes and may tombstone metadata but does not mint the same identifier for a new work.
Schema, lineage and quality internals are referenced or composed from sibling models rather than copied.
Event time and catalogue observation or ingestion time are stored separately whenever they differ.
Access defaults to the declared accessRights; public licences are explicit exceptions to a deny-for-non-public default in internal registers.

read: Public read of descriptive metadata is the default for entries with a public access rights code.
Reading a distribution's payload is governed by the access conditions of that distribution, which may be stricter than the entry's.
Evidence artefacts (validation reports, measurements, sensitivity assessments) are readable by the holder and stewards; publication of them is a holder decision.
Every read of restricted payload is attributable to an identified requester.
create: Only the holder or a delegated steward may create a dataset entry; catalogue operators may create catalogue records but not datasets.
Creation allocates the master-system identifier and records the creation instant as observation time.
Harvested entries are created with an origin code identifying the source catalogue and record.
update: In-place update is permitted for descriptive and registration fields; content-affecting change requires a new version.
Updates record who changed what and when, and preserve the prior value for harvested fields that were overridden locally.
Status and access-level changes require the authorising role named in the entry.
delete: Dataset entries are not deleted; they are deprecated or withdrawn with a tombstone.
Payload deletion is permitted only through an approved retention action with recorded evidence and no active legal hold.
Deletion signals must be propagated to catalogues known to have harvested the record, using the source's declared deleted-record support level.

roles.name: Data holder
responsibilities: Accountable for content, access decisions, licence choice and service level
Approves withdrawal, deletion and access-level changes
Owns fitness-for-use statements and documented limitations

roles.name: Data steward
responsibilities: Maintains descriptive metadata, classification and coverage statements
Runs profile validation and resolves violations
Monitors release cadence, punctuality and schema drift

roles.name: Catalogue operator
responsibilities: Operates the register, its records and its harvesting endpoints
Enforces profile obligations and duplicate detection across federated sources
Publishes tombstones and propagates deletion signals

roles.name: Quality assessor
responsibilities: Computes and records quality measurements against defined metrics
Issues quality certificates and records user feedback annotations
Escalates threshold failures to the holder and steward

roles.name: Privacy and compliance reviewer
responsibilities: Classifies sensitivity and reviews de-identification and disclosure control
Verifies legal basis, retention rules and erasure or hold conflicts
Reviews training-use permissions and bias documentation for AI reuse

roles.name: Consuming agent
responsibilities: Resolves identifiers, verifies fixity and pins the version it consumed
Evaluates access conditions and machine-readable policy before use
Reports defects and reacts to deprecation and breaking-change signals

access.default_rule: Descriptive metadata is readable by default; payload access follows the declared access rights code, and any narrowing of metadata visibility requires an explicit, expiring exception.
exceptions: Sensitivity assessments, residual-risk statements and linkage-risk analyses are holder-and-reviewer scoped even when the dataset is public, because publishing them can enable re-identification.
Endpoint credentials, quota keys and internal service limits within the access-service finding are never exposed in public projections.
Embargoed datasets expose the entry and the embargo end instant but not the distributions until the embargo lapses.
Harvest log entries and local override records are operator-scoped; only the resulting values are public.
Where a jurisdiction forbids publishing an entry at all, a suppression exception is recorded with authority, reason and review date rather than deleting the entry.
Explicit public licence or public accessRights on the dataset or distribution.
Bilateral data-sharing agreement or API access contract naming the requesting agent and purpose.
Embargo expiry that flips accessRights from restricted to public at the available date.
Statutory open-data mandates recorded as applicable legislation.
Legal erasure, court order or security classification that suppresses even metadata that would otherwise be public.
audit_requirements: Every access decision on restricted payload records requester, purpose, decision, approver and RFC 3339 decision time.
Every state transition (status, access level, retirement) records actor, prior value, new value and time.
Every deletion or retention action records approval reference and evidence location and is retained after the payload is gone.
Harvest runs and local overrides are logged so divergence from the source catalogue is reconstructable.
Log identifier minting, status changes, harvest ingest, access decisions, checksum verification failures, withdrawal and erasure with event time and observation time.
Retain audit records of access grants and denials at artifact scope for restricted distributions.
Record the agent, role and policy version used for each exception.

read_order: AGENTS.md - resolve Name, Type and the four URLs before touching any data
Specification URL - the format-neutral model: bundles, layers, findings, data elements and artifact rules
Storage type URL - how the entry is projected into the concrete store (document database, Git tree, RDF store); projections never redefine semantics
Interface URL - the access interface and its authentication, quotas and error semantics
Processes URL - CRUD, versioning, validation, harvest, withdrawal and retention procedures
Declared profile documents - validate before publishing or harvesting

coverage.claim: Covers the asset-level operating surface of a catalogued dataset — identity and registration, classification, coverage, declared structure, distributions and access services, rights and accountability, provenance, versioning and retirement, quality and fitness, and profile interoperability — grounded in DCAT 3, DCAT-AP 3.0.0, DCAT-US, DataCite, Data Package, RO-Crate, Croissant, DQV, PROV-O, OAI-PMH, ODRL, RFC 3339 and named EU legal and statistical sources, plus four operations imported from the Grok result. It claims no conformance to any cited standard, retains security and preservation-packaging as declared gaps, excludes field-level semantics, full lineage graphs, metric definitions and product packaging, and is not complete for domain-specific dataset types or for any jurisdiction beyond those named.

checklist.notes: Master-system identifier first, then governed persistent identifier, then locally minted UUID/ULID; abstract-versus-version granularity and alternate identifiers are explicit questions. Grounded in DCAT 3, DataCite 4.6 and FAIR F1/F3.

Registration state, maturity status, version chaining, deprecation, withdrawal with tombstone and retention actions are separate findings with distinct authorities (DCAT 3, DataCite tombstone guidance, OAI-PMH deleted records).
Series membership, part aggregation, derivation, version chains, successor links, service-serves-dataset and typed related identifiers, each with a relation-type vocabulary question.

Coverage interval, issued/modified, next expected update, generation time, measurement time, harvest datestamp and embargo end are distinguished; RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset is mandated, with event time separated from observation/ingestion time.
